title: Captions, transcripts, and alternatives
learningObjectives: Explain captions, transcripts, and alternatives and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Captions provide text for spoken dialogue and relevant sounds in video. Transcripts provide a text version of audio or audiovisual content. Audio description or equivalent alternatives communicate important visual information that is not available in the audio track.
understand.whyItMatters: Captions and alternatives make learning content usable for deaf and hard-of-hearing users and for people in noisy or quiet environments. They also support searching and review.
understand.analogy: Captions are a readable companion to the audio; transcripts provide the full written route through the content.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The video declares a captions track and links to a transcript. Production assets must provide accurate timing and content.

examples.explanation: The video declares a captions track and links to a transcript. Production assets must provide accurate timing and content.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Prepare captions and a transcript for a short lesson video. Include meaningful sound cues and identify visual information needing description.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.
